description: Maine-only rules checked against Title 29-A of the Maine Revised Statutes. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: In a Maine business or residential district or built-up portion, the maximum rate of speed is
options: 35 mph unless a beacon is flashing
questions.explanation: Section 2074(1)(C), amended by PL 2025, c. 199, sets 25 mph in a business or residential district or built-up portion unless otherwise posted.

questions.q: On Maine public ways that are not covered by the school, intersection, or business-and-residential rates, the maximum is
options: 55 mph even if a lower limit is posted
questions.explanation: Section 2074(1)(D), amended by PL 2025, c. 199, sets 45 mph on all other public ways unless otherwise posted. A posted limit replaces that figure.

questions.q: When the Commissioner of Transportation adjusts a maximum speed, the commissioner may not set a maximum above
options: 75 mph on interstate-type highways, 60 mph otherwise
70 mph inside a city and 80 mph on the Turnpike
questions.explanation: Section 2073(1)(C) says the commissioner may not set maximums that exceed 60 mph or, on the interstate system or other divided controlled-access highways, 75 mph. The commissioner may not set maximums for the Maine Turnpike. Those are ceilings, not the default rates in section 2074.

questions.q: Operating at a speed that exceeds Maine's maximum rate by 30 mph or more is
options: A civil violation only if it occurs in a school zone
Legal on an interstate when no minimum is posted
A violation only after the third offense
questions.explanation: Section 2074, subsection 3, says a person commits a Class E crime by operating a motor vehicle at a speed that exceeds the maximum rate of speed by 30 mph or more. The complaint must specify the alleged speed.

questions.q: Maine's OUI crime includes operating a motor vehicle while having an alcohol level of
options: 0.05 grams or more per 100 milliliters of blood
0.08 grams or more per 100 ml blood or 210 L breath
0.10 grams or more per 210 liters of breath only
questions.explanation: Title 29-A, section 2411, subsection 1-A, paragraph A, prohibits operating under the influence of intoxicants or while having an alcohol level of 0.08 grams or more of alcohol per 100 milliliters of blood or 210 liters of breath.

questions.q: A Maine license condition for a person who has not attained 21 forbids operating a motor vehicle with an alcohol level of
options: 0.02 grams or more per 100 milliliters of blood
More than 0.00 per 100 ml blood or 210 L breath
questions.explanation: Section 2472, subsection 1, states the condition as not operating with an alcohol level of more than 0.00 grams per 100 milliliters of blood or 210 liters of breath. Maine does not use 0.02 as that under-21 figure.

questions.q: A person under 21 who operates a motor vehicle shall submit to a chemical test when there is probable cause to believe the person
options: Refused to show a registration certificate
Drove with any alcohol (over 0.00) or under a covered drug
Was a passenger in a vehicle where alcohol was present
questions.explanation: Section 2472, subsection 4, imposes that duty to submit. The alcohol figure is more than 0.00, matching the license condition in subsection 1. Operated with an alcohol level of more than 0.00 grams per 100 milliliters of blood or 210 liters of breath, or while under the influence of a drug category covered by the section.

questions.q: After a hearing on a juvenile-provisional moving-violation suspension, an individual who has not yet attained 18
options: Must be given a jury trial before the suspension starts
Does not have a right to a hearing
May keep driving if a parent posts a bond
Has the same hearing right as a driver over 21
questions.explanation: Section 2472(2) says that if a hearing is requested the Secretary of State shall provide one as soon as practicable, but an individual who has not yet attained 18 does not have a right to a hearing.

questions.q: A person who is 15 or older may apply for a Maine learner's permit. An applicant who is 15 or older and has not attained 18 must
options: Log 70 hours before the knowledge test
questions.explanation: Section 1304, subsection 1, paragraph A, allows an application at 15 or older and requires driver education before application when the person has not attained 18.

questions.q: A person under 21 may not apply for a Maine license unless six months have passed since the learner's permit was issued and the person has completed at least
questions.explanation: Section 1304(1)(H) requires the six-month period and a minimum of 70 hours, including 10 hours of night driving, accompanied by a parent, guardian, or licensed driver at least 20. A parent, stepparent, guardian, spouse, or employer must certify the time.

questions.q: For 270 days after issuance, a Maine driver under 18 who has been issued a driver's license may not operate between midnight and 5 a.m. and may not
options: Carry non-family passengers without a qualified accompanier
Use a hands-free device while parked off the public way
questions.explanation: Section 1311(1)(A) and (B) state the passenger and midnight-to-5 a.m. limits. Subsection 2 keeps those restrictions in effect for 270 days from issuance, and that period may extend beyond the 18th birthday. The section also defines which non-family residents count as immediate family. Carry passengers other than immediate family members unless accompanied by a licensed operator who meets the learner's-permit accompanier requirements.

questions.q: In Maine, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Maine issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Maine, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Maine requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Maine complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Maine requires 70 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a Maine teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Maine requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

questions.q: In Maine, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Maine, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Maine not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Maine restricts provisional drivers from Midnight to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Maine car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Maine car knowledge test has 30 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Maine car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Maine car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Maine, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Maine, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.

questions.q: In Maine, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Maine sets the under-21 limit at 0.00%.

questions.q: In Maine, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Maine brings a suspension of 275 days.

provenance.manual: Title 29-A, §2521: Implied consent to chemical tests

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Maine?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Maine can be posted up to 75 mph for cars.

questions.q: Which best describes Maine's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Only texting is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Maine: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

provenance.manual: Title 29-A, §2121: Use of mobile telephones and handheld electronic devices while operating motor vehicles prohibited

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Maine?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Maine, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: never allowed.

questions.q: How is Maine's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: Maine seat belt enforcement is primary.

provenance.manual: Title 29-A, §2081: Use of safety seat belts and child restraint systems

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Maine?
questions.explanation: Maine requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

provenance.manual: Title 29-A, §2081: Use of safety seat belts and child restraint systems

questions.q: What is Maine's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Maine requires at least $50,000 / $100,000 / $25,000.

provenance.manual: Insurance Required by Law | PFR Insurance

questions.q: Under Maine's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Maine can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 12 months.
